items.title: The rank-two half-space alternative and the chamber-length induction $(P_n)$, $(Q_n)$
items.statement:
Let $S$ be a finite set, $m$ a Coxeter matrix on $S$, $W$ the group presented by $(S,m)$ with length function $\ell$ ([[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]]), $V=\mathbb R^S$, $B$ the Coxeter form, $\rho:W\to\mathrm{GL}(V)$ the canonical reflection homomorphism with root system $\Phi$ ([[def-cg-canonical-reflection-homomorphism]]), and let $V^*$ be the algebraic dual with its dual action, its chamber $C$, its interior $C^\circ$ and its root hyperplanes $H_\alpha$ ([[def-cg-dual-chambers-and-reflection-hyperplanes]]). For $s\in S$ put
$$B_s:=\{f\in V^*:f(e_s)>0\};$$
then $C^\circ=\bigcap_{s\in S}B_s$ and the translate $sB_s=\{f\in V^*:f(e_s)<0\}$ is the opposite open half-space. For distinct $s,t$ let $W_{s,t}:=\langle s,t\rangle\le W$ be the standard parabolic subgroup, with intrinsic length $\ell_{s,t}$, which agrees with $\ell$ on $W_{s,t}$ ([[thm-hh-parabolic-minimal-representatives-and-length-additivity]] (2)). For $s\ne t$ and $k\ge0$ let $u_k$ be the alternating word $s\,t\,s\cdots$ of $k$ letters beginning with $s$, so $u_0=1$.

**(1) Rank-two half-space alternative.** Let $s\ne t$ and $v\in W_{s,t}$. For each $s'\in\{s,t\}$ exactly one of
$$v(B_s\cap B_t)\subseteq B_{s'},\qquad v(B_s\cap B_t)\subseteq s'B_{s'}$$
holds, and if the second holds then $\ell_{s,t}(s'v)=\ell_{s,t}(v)-1$. Moreover, if $m(s,t)<\infty$ then the elements $u_0,\dots,u_{2m(s,t)-1}$ exhaust $W_{s,t}$, with $\ell_{s,t}(u_k)=\min(k,2m(s,t)-k)$, and the unique element of $W_{s,t}$ having both $s$ and $t$ as left descents is $u_{m(s,t)}$; if $m(s,t)=\infty$ then $\ell_{s,t}(u_k)=k$ for every $k\ge0$, the elements $u_k$ are pairwise distinct, and no element of $W_{s,t}$ has both $s$ and $t$ as left descents.

**(2) The simultaneous induction.** For $n\ge0$ let
$$(\mathrm P_n):\ \text{for all }w\in W\text{ with }\ell(w)=n\text{ and all }s\in S,\ wC^\circ\subseteq B_s\text{, or }wC^\circ\subseteq sB_s\text{ and }\ell(sw)=\ell(w)-1;$$
$$(\mathrm Q_n):\ \text{for all }w\in W\text{ with }\ell(w)=n\text{ and all }s\ne t\text{ there is }u\in W_{s,t}\text{ with }wC^\circ\subseteq u(B_s\cap B_t)\text{ and }\ell(w)=\ell_{s,t}(u)+\ell(u^{-1}w).$$
Then $(\mathrm P_n)$ and $(\mathrm Q_n)$ hold for every $n\ge0$. Explicitly: $(\mathrm P_0)$ and $(\mathrm Q_0)$ are immediate; (1) together with $(\mathrm Q_n)$ yields $(\mathrm P_{n+1})$; and (1) together with $(\mathrm Q_n)$ and $(\mathrm P_m)$ for all $m\le n+1$ yields $(\mathrm Q_{n+1})$.

**(3) Canonical factorisation.** Let $w\in W$ and $s\ne t$. Write $w=u\,d$ with $u\in W_{s,t}$ and $d$ the minimal representative of the right coset $W_{s,t}w$. Then $\ell(w)=\ell(u)+\ell(d)$ and $\ell(s'd)>\ell(d)$ for $s'\in\{s,t\}$ ([[thm-hh-parabolic-minimal-representatives-and-length-additivity]] (3)), and
$$wC^\circ\subseteq u(B_s\cap B_t),\qquad \ell(w)=\ell_{s,t}(u)+\ell(u^{-1}w).$$

**(4) Chamber-descent equivalence.** For every $w\in W$ and $s\in S$ one has $wC^\circ\subseteq B_s$ or $wC^\circ\subseteq sB_s$; moreover
$$wC^\circ\subseteq sB_s\iff \ell(sw)<\ell(w).$$
items.strategy:
**Part (1).** (a) Reduction to the rank-two plane. By [[lem-cg-dual-action-and-chamber-faces-exist]] (3) the subgroup $W_{s,t}$ preserves $P:=\mathbb Re_s+\mathbb Re_t\subseteq V$ and its dual plane $P^*$, and its action realises the two standard dihedral pictures: in the finite case the $2m(s,t)$ chambers $wC_P$ ($w\in W_{s,t}$), $C_P=\{f\in P^*:f(e_s),f(e_t)\ge0\}$, are the closed sectors cut out by the $m$ root lines $H_\beta\cap P^*$ ($\beta\in\Phi_P=W_{s,t}\{e_s,e_t\}$), they have pairwise disjoint interiors, tile $P^*$, are permuted simply transitively by $W_{s,t}$, and any two distinct ones are separated by a root line; in the infinite case the chambers tile $\{f:f(e_s+e_t)>0\}\cup\{0\}$ (the nonzero points of the boundary line lie in no chamber), and their traces on the affine line $f(e_s+e_t)=1$ are exactly the intervals $[j,j+1]$, $j\in\mathbb Z$, with the root traces the integers ([[lem-cg-dual-action-and-chamber-faces-exist]] (3)(i)-(ii); [[def-cg-real-coxeter-form-and-reflection]] for $c(s,t)$). Since $\rho(v)$ preserves $P$ and fixes $P^\perp$ pointwise for every $v\in W_{s,t}$ ([[lem-cg-reflection-form-invariance-and-rank-two-orders]] (3)(ii), where $P^\perp=\{u:B(u,e_s)=B(u,e_t)=0\}$), the restriction map $\pi:V^*\to P^*$, $f\mapsto f|_P$, is surjective and $W_{s,t}$-equivariant (for $x\in P$ both $(v\cdot f)(x)$ and $(v\cdot(f|_P))(x)$ evaluate at $\rho(v)^{-1}x\in P$), and satisfies $B_s\cap B_t=\pi^{-1}(C_P^\circ)$ and $B_{s'}=\pi^{-1}\{f\in P^*:f(e_{s'})>0\}$ for $s'\in\{s,t\}$; hence $v(B_s\cap B_t)\subseteq B_{s'}$ if and only if $vC_P^\circ$ lies in the open half-plane $\{f\in P^*:f(e_{s'})>0\}$, and $v(B_s\cap B_t)\subseteq s'B_{s'}$ if and only if $vC_P^\circ$ lies in the opposite open half-plane. Now $vC_P^\circ$ is open and connected and meets no root line (its points are interiors of sectors), in particular it does not meet the line $H_{e_{s'}}\cap P^*$; as an open connected set disjoint from a hyperplane it lies in exactly one of the two open half-planes. This gives the dichotomy; the cylinder description shows that the two alternatives are exactly 'positive' and 'negative' side of $H_{e_{s'}}$.
(b) Lengths. Consecutive $u_k$ differ by right multiplication by a generator $r$; applying $u_k$ to the common wall of $C_P$ and $rC_P$ proves adjacency. The distinct Cayley-cycle vertices therefore list the finite sectors in cyclic order; the elements $u_k$ with $k\le m(s,t)$ are reduced with $\ell_{s,t}(u_k)=k$, the relations $u_{k+2m}=u_k$ hold in the finite case, and $\ell_{s,t}(u_k)=k$ for all $k\ge0$ in the infinite case ([[lem-hh-dihedral-root-recurrence-and-root-sign]] (3),(4),(7); intrinsic length equals ambient length by [[thm-hh-parabolic-minimal-representatives-and-length-additivity]] (2); in the finite case $u_0,\dots,u_{2m-1}$ are the vertices of the displayed Cayley cycle (connected and 2-regular), so $\ell_{s,t}(u_k)=\min(k,2m-k)$ is the graph distance from $u_0$). The substitutions $su_k=u_{1-k}$ and $tu_k=u_{-1-k}$ (indices modulo $2m$; for $m=\infty$, on the interval index $j$ of the traces, $s$ acts by $j\mapsto -j-1$ and $t$ by $j\mapsto 1-j$, read off from the displayed generator matrices of [[lem-cg-dual-action-and-chamber-faces-exist]] (3)) combine with the simple transitivity to give: the wall $H_{e_s}$ separates $C_P^\circ$ from $u_kC_P^\circ$ precisely when $k\in\{1,\dots,m\}$, and $H_{e_t}$ precisely when $k\in\{m,\dots,2m-1\}$ (finite case; in the infinite case precisely when $j\le-1$, respectively $j\ge1$). Hence left multiplication by $s'$ shortens exactly when the chamber lies on the $s'$-negative side, both descents occur only for $k=m$ in the finite case and never in the infinite case, and by the simple transitivity every finite-type $v$ is some $u_k$, and every infinite-type $v$ has its displayed integer interval index; this is the length clause of (1).
**Part (2).** $(\mathrm P_0)$ and $(\mathrm Q_0)$ are immediate since $C^\circ\subseteq B_s$ for every $s$. $(\mathrm P_{n+1})$: let $\ell(w)=n+1$ and $s\in S$, and pick $t$ with $w=tw'$, $\ell(w')=n$. For rank at least two, $(\mathrm Q_n)$ already implies $(\mathrm P_n)$: apply its factorisation to a length-$n$ element and a pair containing the tested generator, and use the negative rank-two alternative plus subadditivity to force a descent. Empty and rank-one systems are immediate from $W=\{1\}$ or $W=\{1,s\}$ and $sB_s$; no pair is needed. Thus the first conditional uses $(\mathrm Q_n)$ alone. If $s=t$ then the resulting $(\mathrm P_n)$ applied to $w'$ gives $w'C^\circ\subseteq B_s$ (the second alternative would give $\ell(sw')=\ell(w')-1$, i.e. $\ell(w)=n-1$, a contradiction), so $wC^\circ=t(w'C^\circ)\subseteq tB_s=sB_s$ and $\ell(sw)=\ell(w')=n=\ell(w)-1$, the second alternative. If $s\ne t$, apply $(\mathrm Q_n)$ to $w'$: there is $u\in W_{s,t}$ with $w'C^\circ\subseteq u(B_s\cap B_t)$ and $\ell(w')=\ell_{s,t}(u)+\ell(u^{-1}w')$. Put $v:=tu\in W_{s,t}$. In case (a) of (1) for $s'=s$, $wC^\circ\subseteq tu(B_s\cap B_t)\subseteq B_s$. In case (b), $wC^\circ\subseteq sB_s$ and, using subadditivity of $\ell$, $\ell\le\ell_{s,t}$ on $W_{s,t}$, and the length clause of (1),
$$\ell(sw)=\ell(stw')\le\ell_{s,t}(stu)+\ell(u^{-1}w')=\ell_{s,t}(tu)-1+\ell(u^{-1}w')\le\ell_{s,t}(u)+\ell(u^{-1}w')=\ell(w')=\ell(w)-1,$$
while $\ell(sw)\ge\ell(w)-1$ by the length-parity clause of [[thm-hh-coxeter-exchange-deletion-and-faithfulness]] (1); hence $\ell(sw)=\ell(w)-1$. $(\mathrm Q_{n+1})$: let $\ell(w)=n+1$, $s\ne t$, and factor $w=u\,d$ as in (3); by the parabolic theorem $\ell(w)=\ell(u)+\ell(d)$ and $\ell(s'd)>\ell(d)$ for $s'\in\{s,t\}$. For each $s'\in\{s,t\}$ apply $(\mathrm P_{\ell(d)})$ to $d$; it is available because $\ell(d)\le n+1$ and the induction proves $(\mathrm P_m)$ for all $m\le n+1$ before $(\mathrm Q_{n+1})$: if $dC^\circ\subseteq s'B_{s'}$ then $\ell(s'd)=\ell(d)-1$, contradicting $\ell(s'd)>\ell(d)$; hence $dC^\circ\subseteq B_{s'}$. Therefore $dC^\circ\subseteq B_s\cap B_t$ and $wC^\circ=u(dC^\circ)\subseteq u(B_s\cap B_t)$, with $\ell(w)=\ell(u)+\ell(d)=\ell_{s,t}(u)+\ell(u^{-1}w)$. The induction on $n$ ([[thm-induction-principle]]) proves both families, and (3) is what was just proved.
**Part (4).** The dichotomy is $(\mathrm P_n)$ for $n=\ell(w)$. For the equivalence: if $wC^\circ\subseteq sB_s$ then $(\mathrm P_n)$ gives $\ell(sw)<\ell(w)$. Conversely, suppose $\ell(sw)<\ell(w)$ and put $w':=sw$, so $\ell(w')=\ell(w)-1$ and $w=sw'$; applying $(\mathrm P)$ to $w'$ gives $w'C^\circ\subseteq B_s$ or $sB_s$, and the second case implies $\ell(sw')=\ell(w')-1$, i.e. $\ell(w)=\ell(w')-1$, impossible; hence $w'C^\circ\subseteq B_s$, and applying the bijection $\rho(s)^*$ gives $wC^\circ=s(w'C^\circ)\subseteq sB_s$.

items.title: Root sign coherence and the action of simple reflections on positive roots
items.statement:
Let $S$ be a finite set, $m$ a Coxeter matrix, $W$ the presented group ([[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]]), $V=\mathbb R^S$ with Coxeter form $B$, the reflections $r_a$ ([[def-cg-real-coxeter-form-and-reflection]]), the canonical reflection homomorphism $\rho:W\to\mathrm{GL}(V)$, the root system $\Phi=\{\rho(w)e_s\}$, the reflections $T$, and the positive cone $V_+=\{\sum_s\lambda_se_s:\lambda_s\ge0\}$ ([[def-cg-canonical-reflection-homomorphism]]); every root satisfies $B(\alpha,\alpha)=1$ ([[lem-cg-reflection-representation-descends-and-root-norms]] (3)). Let $C,C^\circ$ be the chamber and its interior of the dual action and put $B_s:=\{f\in V^*:f(e_s)>0\}$ ([[def-cg-dual-chambers-and-reflection-hyperplanes]]).

**(1) Sign criterion for the cone.** For $v\in V$: $v\in V_+\setminus\{0\}$ if and only if $f(v)>0$ for every $f\in C^\circ$.

**(2) Roots have a sign.** Every root $\alpha\in\Phi$ lies in $V_+\setminus\{0\}$ or in $-V_+\setminus\{0\}$, and not in both. Hence, with
$$\Phi_+:=\Phi\cap V_+,\qquad \Phi_-:=\Phi\cap(-V_+),$$
one has $\Phi=\Phi_+\sqcup\Phi_-$, $\Phi_-=-\Phi_+$, $e_s\in\Phi_+$ for every $s\in S$, and for every $w\in W$ and $s\in S$
$$\rho(w)e_s\in\Phi_+\iff w^{-1}C^\circ\subseteq B_s,\qquad \rho(w)e_s\in\Phi_-\iff w^{-1}C^\circ\subseteq sB_s.$$
In particular $f(\alpha)>0$ for all $f\in C^\circ$ when $\alpha\in\Phi_+$, and $f(\alpha)<0$ for all $f\in C^\circ$ when $\alpha\in\Phi_-$.

**(3) Simple reflections act on positive roots.** For every $s\in S$,
$$r_s(\Phi_+\setminus\{e_s\})=\Phi_+\setminus\{e_s\},\qquad r_se_s=-e_s,\qquad r_s\Phi=\Phi;$$
equivalently $r_s\Phi_+=(\Phi_+\setminus\{e_s\})\cup\{-e_s\}$.

**(1)** If $v=\sum_s\lambda_se_s$ with $\lambda_s\ge0$ and $v

otin V_+$ then some $\lambda_r<0$; let $f_r$ be the dual basis functional of $(e_s)$ ([[lem-cg-dual-action-and-chamber-faces-exist]] (2) exhibits the $f_r$ and $f_r\ge0$), so $f_r(v)=\lambda_r<0$. Then for every $\varepsilon>0$ the functional $f_r+\varepsilon\sum_sf_s$ lies in $C^\circ$, and its value at $v$ is $\lambda_r+\varepsilon\sum_sv(s)<0$ for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon$; hence some element of $C^\circ$ evaluates $v$ negatively. This proves the equivalence.
**(2)** (a) For fixed $w,s$, $(w^{-1}\cdot f)(e_s)=f(ho(w)e_s)$ for all $f\in V^*$, by the definition of the dual action. By $(\mathrm P)$ applied to the element $w^{-1}$ ([[lem-cg-rank-two-prefix-and-chamber-length-induction]] (2)), $w^{-1}C^\circ\subseteq B_s$ or $w^{-1}C^\circ\subseteq sB_s$; these two cases read as $f(ho(w)e_s)>0$ for all $f\in C^\circ$, respectively $f(ho(w)e_s)<0$ for all $f\in C^\circ$. By (1) the root $ho(w)e_s$ lies in $V_+\setminus\{0\}$ or in $-V_+\setminus\{0\}$ accordingly, in particular never in both. As every root is of this form, $\Phi=\Phi_+\cup\Phi_-$; the two parts are exclusive because $V_+\cap(-V_+)=\{0\}$ while $B(\alpha,\alpha)=1$ prevents $\alpha=0$ ([[lem-cg-reflection-representation-descends-and-root-norms]] (3)). Taking $w=1$ gives $e_s\in\Phi_+$ and, reading the equivalence, the displayed characterizations. $\Phi_-=-\Phi_+$ is immediate from the definitions.
**(3)** $r_se_s=-e_s$ is [[lem-cg-reflection-form-invariance-and-rank-two-orders]] (2) with $a=e_s$, $B(e_s,e_s)=1$. Let $\alpha\in\Phi_+\setminus\{e_s\}$. Since $r_s=ho(s)$ and $\Phi$ is $ho(W)$-invariant, $r_s\alpha\in\Phi$, so by (2) either $r_s\alpha\in\Phi_+$ or $r_s\alpha\in\Phi_-$; suppose the latter. With $r_s\alpha=\alpha-2B(\alpha,e_s)e_s$ (the reflection formula, [[def-cg-real-coxeter-form-and-reflection]] (3)) the coordinates in the basis $(e_r)_{r\in S}$ satisfy $(r_s\alpha)(r)=\alpha(r)$ for $r

Hence $r_s\alpha\in\Phi_+$. Since $r_s$ is an involution of $\Phi$ (it is $ho(s)$ and $ho(s)^2=1$ with $r_s\Phi=\Phi$) mapping $e_s$ to $-e_s$, it maps $\Phi_+\setminus\{e_s\}$ bijectively onto $\Phi_+\setminus\{e_s\}$ and $\Phi_+$ onto $(\Phi_+\setminus\{e_s\})\cup\{-e_s\}$.

items.title: The root-length criterion and faithfulness of the canonical reflection representation
items.statement:
Let $S$ be a finite set, $m$ a Coxeter matrix, $W$ the presented group with length function $\ell$ ([[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]]), $V=\mathbb R^S$ with Coxeter form $B$ and canonical reflection homomorphism $\rho:W\to\mathrm{GL}(V)$ with root system $\Phi$ ([[def-cg-canonical-reflection-homomorphism]]), and let $\Phi_+,\Phi_-$ be the positive and negative roots and $C^\circ$ the open chamber of the dual action ([[thm-cg-root-sign-and-simple-reflection-positivity]]).

**(1) Root-length criterion.** For all $w\in W$ and $s\in S$,
$$\ell(ws)>\ell(w)\iff\rho(w)e_s\in\Phi_+,\qquad \ell(ws)<\ell(w)\iff\rho(w)e_s\in\Phi_-.$$

**(2) Disjoint chambers.** If $wC^\circ\cap C^\circ\ne\emptyset$ for some $w\in W$, then $w=1$. Equivalently, the chambers $wC^\circ$ ($w\in W$) are pairwise disjoint and $C^\circ$ is prefundamental for the $W$-action on $V^*$.

**(3) Faithfulness.** The homomorphism $\rho$ is injective, the dual action $W\to\mathrm{GL}(V^*)$ is injective, and for every $w\ne1$ there is $s\in S$ with $\rho(w)e_s\in\Phi_-$.

**(1)** Fix $w\in W$, $s\in S$. By [[thm-cg-root-sign-and-simple-reflection-positivity]] (2), $ho(w)e_s\in\Phi_-$ if and only if $w^{-1}C^\circ\subseteq sB_s$; by the chamber-descent equivalence of [[lem-cg-rank-two-prefix-and-chamber-length-induction]] (4) applied to the element $w^{-1}$ and the generator $s$, this holds if and only if $\ell(s\,w^{-1})=\ell(w^{-1})-1$. Since $(sw^{-1})^{-1}=ws$ and $\ell$ is invariant under inversion ([[thm-hh-parabolic-minimal-representatives-and-length-additivity]] (3), by inversion $w\mapsto w^{-1}$ preserves lengths), this is equivalent to $\ell(ws)=\ell(w)-1$. Finally $\ell(ws)=\ell(w)\pm1$ ([[thm-hh-coxeter-exchange-deletion-and-faithfulness]] (1)) and $\Phi=\Phi_+\sqcup\Phi_-$ ([[thm-cg-root-sign-and-simple-reflection-positivity]] (2)), so the two displayed equivalences are equivalent and both follow.

Since $C^\circ\subseteq B_s$ and $B_s\cap sB_s=\emptyset$, the nonempty intersection shows $wC^\circ

items.title: The geometric inversion set $N(w)$ of a Coxeter element and its step recursion
items.statement:
Let $S$ be a finite set, $m$ a Coxeter matrix, $W$ the presented group with length function $\ell$ ([[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]]), $V=\mathbb R^S$ with Coxeter form $B$ and canonical reflection homomorphism $\rho:W\to\mathrm{GL}(V)$ ([[def-cg-canonical-reflection-homomorphism]]), and let $\Phi=\Phi_+\sqcup\Phi_-$ be the signed root system ([[thm-cg-root-sign-and-simple-reflection-positivity]]).

**(1) Definition.** For $w\in W$ the **inversion set** of $w$ is
$$N(w):=\{\alpha\in\Phi_+:\rho(w)\alpha\in\Phi_-\}=\Phi_+\cap\rho(w)^{-1}\Phi_-.$$
Its elements are the roots inverted by $w$. This is a subset of $\Phi_+$, defined before any finiteness or independence assertion; by construction $\rho(w)N(w)\subseteq\Phi_-$, and $N(w)$ is determined by the linear map $\rho(w)$.

**(2) Elementary identities.** $N(1)=\emptyset$; for every $w\in W$
$$N(w^{-1})=-\rho(w)\,N(w),$$
and consequently $|N(w^{-1})|=|N(w)|$ whenever one of the two sets is finite. For every $u\in W$ and $s\in S$, with $sN(u):=\{\rho(s)\beta:\beta\in N(u)\}$,
$$\ell(us)>\ell(u)\ \Longrightarrow\ N(us)=\{e_s\}\sqcup sN(u),\qquad \ell(us)<\ell(u)\ \Longrightarrow\ N(us)=s\,(N(u)\setminus\{e_s\});$$
in the first case $sN(u)\subseteq\Phi_+\setminus\{e_s\}$ and $e_s\notin N(u)$, so the union is disjoint.

**(3) Convention on reduced words.** We keep the left action $\rho$ of $W$ on $V$. If $w=s_1\cdots s_n$ is a reduced expression, then the **suffix roots** $\rho(s_{i+1}\cdots s_n)^{-1}e_{s_i}$ $(1\le i\le n)$ are elements of $N(w)$, and the **prefix roots** $\rho(s_1\cdots s_{i-1})e_{s_i}$ are elements of $N(w^{-1})$. That these lists are exactly $N(w)$ and $N(w^{-1})$, that their elements are pairwise distinct positive roots, and that in particular $|N(w)|=\ell(w)$, is proved in [[thm-cg-root-inversion-formulas-and-strong-exchange]]; no finiteness or independence beyond the identities of (2) is asserted here.
items.strategy: A definition item. $N(w)$ is defined by a predicate on the set $\Phi_+$ and is therefore well defined; the displayed equality $N(w)=\Phi_+\cap\rho(w)^{-1}\Phi_-$ is the definition unfolded, using $\Phi=\Phi_+\sqcup\Phi_-$ ([[thm-cg-root-sign-and-simple-reflection-positivity]] (2)). Identity (2), first part: $\alpha\in N(w^{-1})$ means $\alpha\in\Phi_+$ and $\rho(w)^{-1}\alpha\in\Phi_-$; writing $\beta:=\rho(w)^{-1}(-\alpha)\in\Phi_+$ (negation swaps $\Phi_\pm$), one has $\rho(w)\beta=-\alpha\in\Phi_-$, so $\beta\in N(w)$ and $\alpha=-\rho(w)\beta$; conversely $-\rho(w)\beta\in\Phi_+$ and $\rho(w)^{-1}(-\rho(w)\beta)=-\beta\in\Phi_-$ for $\beta\in N(w)$. The map $\beta\mapsto-\rho(w)\beta$ is a bijection, giving (2) and the cardinality statement. The step recursion: let $u\in W$, $s\in S$ and assume first $\ell(us)>\ell(u)$. For $\beta\in\Phi_+$ compute $us(\beta)=u(s(\beta))$ in the geometric representation. If $\beta=e_s$, then $us(e_s)=u(-e_s)=-u(e_s)$ and $u(e_s)\in\Phi_+$ by the root-length criterion ([[thm-cg-root-length-criterion-and-faithfulness]] (1)), so $e_s\in N(us)$; also $e_s\notin N(u)$ by the same criterion, since $u(e_s)\in\Phi_+$. If $\beta\ne e_s$ then $s(\beta)\in\Phi_+\setminus\{e_s\}$ by [[thm-cg-root-sign-and-simple-reflection-positivity]] (3), and $s(e_s)=-e_s$; hence $\beta\in N(us)$ if and only if $s(\beta)\in N(u)$, and $\beta\mapsto s(\beta)$ is a bijection of $\Phi_+\setminus\{e_s\}$ onto itself. Therefore $N(us)=\{e_s\}\sqcup sN(u)$, with $sN(u)\subseteq\Phi_+\setminus\{e_s\}$. If $\ell(us)<\ell(u)$, apply the first case to the pair $(us,s)$; here $(us)s=u$ and $\ell(u)>\ell(us)$, so $N(u)=\{e_s\}\sqcup sN(us)$, whence $N(us)=s(N(u)\setminus\{e_s\})$. Finally, for (3): given a reduced expression $w=s_1\cdots s_n$, put $w_i:=s_1\cdots s_i$ and $\alpha_i:=\rho(s_{i+1}\cdots s_n)^{-1}e_{s_i}$; then, since $(s_1\cdots s_n)(s_{i+1}\cdots s_n)^{-1}=s_1\cdots s_i$, one has $\rho(w)\alpha_i=\rho(s_1\cdots s_i)e_{s_i}=-\rho(s_1\cdots s_{i-1})e_{s_i}$, and the prefix root $\rho(s_1\cdots s_{i-1})e_{s_i}$ is positive by the root-length criterion because $\ell(w_{i-1}s_i)=i>\ell(w_{i-1})$; hence $\alpha_i\in N(w)$. The same computation applied to the reversed reduced expression of $w^{-1}$ gives the prefix-root statement for $N(w^{-1})$.

items.title: The root-reflection dictionary, the inversion-set formula, and strong exchange
items.statement:
Let $S$ be a finite set, $m$ a Coxeter matrix, $W$ the presented group with length $\ell$ ([[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]]), $V=\mathbb R^S$ with Coxeter form $B$, canonical reflection homomorphism $\rho$, root system $\Phi=\Phi_+\sqcup\Phi_-$ and reflection set $T=\{wsw^{-1}:w\in W,\ s\in S\}$ ([[def-cg-canonical-reflection-homomorphism]], [[thm-cg-root-sign-and-simple-reflection-positivity]]); every root has $B$-norm one.

**(1) The root-reflection dictionary.** For $\alpha\in\Phi$ choose $w\in W$, $s\in S$ with $\alpha=\rho(w)e_s$ and put $t_\alpha:=wsw^{-1}\in T$. Then:
(i) $t_\alpha$ is independent of the chosen representation of $\alpha$;
(ii) $\rho(t_\alpha)=r_\alpha$, the reflection with normal $\alpha$; and $t_{\rho(w)\alpha}=w\,t_\alpha\,w^{-1}$ for all $w\in W$, $\alpha\in\Phi$;
(iii) $t_{-\alpha}=t_\alpha$, and for $\alpha,\beta\in\Phi$ one has $t_\alpha=t_\beta$ if and only if $\alpha=\pm\beta$;
(iv) the induced map $\{\pm\alpha:\alpha\in\Phi\}\to T$ is a bijection; so is the map $\Phi_+\to T$, $\alpha\mapsto t_\alpha$.

**(2) Inversion formula.** For every $w\in W$ one has $|N(w)|=\ell(w)$ (with $N$ as in [[def-cg-geometric-inversion-set]]); and for every reduced expression $w=s_1\cdots s_n$,
$$N(w)=\bigl\{\rho(s_{i+1}\cdots s_n)^{-1}e_{s_i}:1\le i\le n\bigr\},\qquad N(w^{-1})=\bigl\{\rho(s_1\cdots s_{i-1})e_{s_i}:1\le i\le n\bigr\},$$
the displayed elements being pairwise distinct positive roots.

**(3) Strong exchange.** Let $w\in W$ and $t\in T$ satisfy $\ell(tw)<\ell(w)$, and let $w=s_1\cdots s_n$ be a reduced expression. Then there is a unique $i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$ with
$$tw=s_1\cdots\widehat{s_i}\cdots s_n,\qquad t=r_i:=s_1\cdots s_{i-1}s_is_{i-1}\cdots s_1;$$
moreover, if $\alpha\in\Phi_+$ is the positive root with $t=t_\alpha$, then $\alpha\in N(w^{-1})$ and $\alpha=\rho(s_1\cdots s_{i-1})e_{s_i}$.
items.strategy:
**(1)** (i) If $\alpha=\rho(w)e_s=\rho(w')e_{s'}$, then $\rho(wsw^{-1})=r_{\rho(w)e_s}=r_\alpha=r_{\rho(w')e_{s'}}=\rho(w's'w'^{-1})$ ([[lem-cg-reflection-representation-descends-and-root-norms]] (4)), and faithfulness of $\rho$ ([[thm-cg-root-length-criterion-and-faithfulness]] (3)) gives $wsw^{-1}=w's'w'^{-1}$. (ii) The first identity is the same computation read backwards; for the second write $\alpha=\rho(x)e_s$ and $\rho(w)\alpha=\rho(wx)e_s$, so $t_{\rho(w)\alpha}=(wx)s(wx)^{-1}=w(xsx^{-1})w^{-1}=wt_\alpha w^{-1}$. (iii) Since $\rho(ws)e_s=\rho(w)(-e_s)=-\rho(w)e_s$, the root $-\alpha$ has the representation $\rho(ws)e_s$, so $t_{-\alpha}=(ws)s(ws)^{-1}=wsw^{-1}=t_\alpha$; if $t_\alpha=t_\beta$ then $r_\alpha=r_\beta$ by (ii), and the $(-1)$-eigenspace of $r_\gamma$ is exactly $\mathbb R\gamma$ ([[lem-cg-reflection-form-invariance-and-rank-two-orders]] (2): $r_\gamma\gamma=-\gamma$ and $r_\gamma$ fixes $\ker B(-,\gamma)$ pointwise, and $V=\mathbb R\gamma\oplus\ker B(-,\gamma)$ since $B(\gamma,\gamma)=1$); hence $\beta=\lambda\alpha$ and $1=B(\beta,\beta)=\lambda^2B(\alpha,\alpha)$ gives $\lambda=\pm1$. (iv) Surjectivity onto $T$: $wsw^{-1}=t_{\rho(w)e_s}$; injectivity on $\pm$-classes is (iii); every $\pm$-class of roots has a positive representative by [[thm-cg-root-sign-and-simple-reflection-positivity]] (2), so $\Phi_+\to T$ is a bijection as well.
**(2)** Induction on $\ell(w)$ using the step recursion of [[def-cg-geometric-inversion-set]] (2), which for a reduced word $w=s_1\cdots s_n$ and its prefix $w_{n-1}:=s_1\cdots s_{n-1}$ gives $N(w)=\{e_{s_n}\}\sqcup s_nN(w_{n-1})$ because $\ell(w)=\ell(w_{n-1})+1$. The two parts are disjoint, so $|N(w)|=|N(w_{n-1})|+1$; with the base cases $N(1)=\emptyset$ (giving $|N(s)|=1$) induction yields $|N(w)|=\ell(w)$. Iterating the recursion yields $N(w)=\{e_{s_n}\}\sqcup s_n\{e_{s_{n-1}}\}\sqcup s_ns_{n-1}\{e_{s_{n-2}}\}\sqcup\cdots=\{s_n\cdots s_{i+1}e_{s_i}:1\le i\le n\}$, i.e. the displayed suffix-root list, whose elements are therefore distinct and lie in $N(w)$; applying the same formula to the reversed reduced expression of $w^{-1}$ (reversal is length-preserving for reduced words) gives the prefix-root formula for $N(w^{-1})$.
**(3)** Keep the notation of (2) and put $r_i:=s_1\cdots s_{i-1}s_is_{i-1}\cdots s_1$ for $1\le i\le n$; these are the prefix reflections of the reduced word, and the set $\Phi(w):=\{r\in T:\eta(r,w)=-1\}$ of [[lem-hh-dihedral-root-recurrence-and-root-sign]] (6)(b),(c) equals $\{r_1,\dots,r_n\}$: it is independent of the reduced expression, the $r_i$ are pairwise distinct, and $\#\Phi(w)=\ell(w)$. For each $i$, direct cancellation gives $r_iw=w_{i-1}s_iw_{i-1}^{-1}w_{i-1}s_is_{i+1}\cdots s_n=w_{i-1}s_{i+1}\cdots s_n=s_1\cdots\widehat{s_i}\cdots s_n$, so $\ell(r_iw)<\ell(w)$ and every element of $\Phi(w)$ shortens $w$ from the left with deletion of one letter. Conversely, if $\ell(rw)<\ell(w)$ then $\eta(r,w)=-1$: suppose $\eta(r,w)=+1$; from the cocycle identity $\eta(r,uv)=\eta(r,u)\eta(u^{-1}ru,v)$ built into (6)(b) one computes $\eta(r,r)=-1$ (indeed $(\varepsilon,r)\cdot r=(-\varepsilon,r)$, as follows by writing $r=usu^{-1}$ and using the cocycle twice, together with $\eta(w^{-1}rw,w^{-1})=\eta(r,w)$) and hence $\eta(r,rw)=\eta(r,r)\eta(r^{-1}rr,w)=-\eta(r,w)=-1$; so $r\in\Phi(rw)$, i.e. $r=r_j$ for some prefix reflection of a reduced word of $rw$, and the previous paragraph gives $\ell(w)=\ell(r\cdot rw)<\ell(rw)$, contradicting $\ell(rw)<\ell(w)$. Therefore $r\in\Phi(w)=\{r_1,\dots,r_n\}$, so $r=r_i$ for a unique $i$ (pairwise distinctness) and $tw=rw=s_1\cdots\widehat{s_i}\cdots s_n$. For the root clause: $t=r_i$ is the reflection $w_{i-1}s_iw_{i-1}^{-1}$ with normal $\rho(w_{i-1})e_{s_i}=\rho(s_1\cdots s_{i-1})e_{s_i}$, so by (1) the positive root $\alpha$ with $t=t_\alpha$ is exactly that prefix root, and it lies in $N(w^{-1})$ by (2).

items.title: Roots, inversions and chamber images in $I_2(5)$, $A_2$ and infinite dihedral type
items.statement:
Let $S=\{s,t\}$ with $m:=m(s,t)\in\{3,5,\infty\}$, $V=\mathbb R^S$, and let $B$ be the Coxeter form with $c=\cos(\pi/m)$ for $m<\infty$ and $c=1$ for $m=\infty$, so that $B(e_s,e_s)=B(e_t,e_t)=1$ and $B(e_s,e_t)=-c$ ([[def-cg-real-coxeter-form-and-reflection]]). Let $\rho,\Phi,\Phi_\pm,N,C^\circ,W,\ell$ be as on this page ([[def-cg-canonical-reflection-homomorphism]], [[thm-cg-root-sign-and-simple-reflection-positivity]], [[def-cg-geometric-inversion-set]], [[thm-cg-root-inversion-formulas-and-strong-exchange]]), and let $u_k$ denote the alternating word $s\,t\,s\cdots$ of $k$ letters. The following data are computed and verified.

**(i) $A_2=I_2(3)$.** $c=\tfrac12$ and $\Phi_+=\{e_s,\ e_t,\ e_s+e_t\}$. For the six elements,
$$N(1)=\emptyset,\quad N(s)=\{e_s\},\quad N(t)=\{e_t\},\quad N(st)=\{e_t,\,e_s+e_t\},\quad N(ts)=\{e_s,\,e_s+e_t\},\quad N(sts)=\Phi_+,$$
each of cardinality $\ell(w)$. In the dual plane $V^*$ the three walls $H_{e_s},H_{e_t},H_{e_s+e_t}$ cut out six sectors, and the six chambers $wC^\circ$ occur in the cyclic order $C^\circ,\ sC^\circ,\ stC^\circ,\ stsC^\circ,\ tsC^\circ,\ tC^\circ$, with $stsC^\circ=-C^\circ$; explicitly $H_{e_s}$ separates $C^\circ$ from $u_1C^\circ,\dots,u_3C^\circ$ and $H_{e_t}$ from $u_3C^\circ,\dots,u_5C^\circ$.

**(ii) $I_2(5)$.** $2c=\phi=\tfrac{1+\sqrt5}{2}$, $4c^2-1=\phi$, and
$$\Phi_+=\{e_s,\ e_t,\ e_t+\phi e_s,\ e_s+\phi e_t,\ \phi(e_s+e_t)\},$$
five roots, each of $B$-norm one. With $\ell(u_k)=\min(k,10-k)$ for $0\le k<10$, for $1\le k\le5$
$$N(u_1)=\{e_s\},\quad N(u_2)=\{e_t,\,e_s+\phi e_t\},\quad N(u_3)=\{e_s,\,e_t+\phi e_s,\,\phi(e_s+e_t)\},$$
$$N(u_4)=\{e_t,\,e_s+\phi e_t,\,\phi(e_s+e_t),\,\phi e_s+e_t\},\quad N(u_5)=\Phi_+,$$
and for $5\le k<10$ one has $N(u_k)=\Phi_+\setminus N(u_{k-5}')$, where $u_j'$ is the alternating word of length $j$ beginning with $t$; for instance $N(u_7)=\{e_t,\,e_s+\phi e_t,\,\phi(e_s+e_t)\}$, of cardinality $3=\ell(u_7)$. The ten chambers $u_kC^\circ$ are the sectors cut out by the five root lines; the chambers on the negative side of $H_{e_s}$ are exactly $u_1C^\circ,\dots,u_5C^\circ$, and those on the negative side of $H_{e_t}$ are exactly $u_5C^\circ,\dots,u_9C^\circ$.

**(iii) $I_2(\infty)$.** $c=1$. Put $u:=e_s+e_t$; then $B(u,\cdot)=0$ on $\mathbb Re_s+\mathbb Re_t$, and
$$\Phi_+=\{e_s+ku:k\ge0\}\cup\{e_t+ku:k\ge0\}$$
is infinite. For every $k\ge0$,
$$N((st)^k)=\{ju+e_t:0\le j\le 2k-1\},\qquad N((st)^ks)=\{ju+e_s:0\le j\le 2k\},$$
of cardinalities $2k=\ell((st)^k)$ and $2k+1=\ell((st)^ks)$. The chambers $wC^\circ$ are the cones over the intervals $(j,j+1)$ of the affine line $\{f:f(e_s)+f(e_t)=1\}$, and the walls $H_{e_s},H_{e_t}$ meet that line in the points $0$ and $1$.
items.strategy:
All assertions are substitutions into the general results, using $\rho(s)e_t=e_t+2ce_s$, $\rho(t)e_s=e_s+2ce_t$ ([[def-cg-real-coxeter-form-and-reflection]] (3)). 
(i) $\rho(s)e_t=e_t+e_s$ and $\rho(t)e_s=e_s+e_t$, so the six roots $\pm e_s,\pm e_t,\pm(e_s+e_t)$ have $B$-norm one; the sets $N$ are read off from the step recursion of [[def-cg-geometric-inversion-set]] (2): $N(s)=\{e_s\}$, $N(st)=\{e_t\}\sqcup t\{e_s\}=\{e_t,e_s+e_t\}$, $N(ts)=\{e_s\}\sqcup s\{e_t\}=\{e_s,e_s+e_t\}$, $N(sts)=\{e_s\}\sqcup s\{e_t,e_s+e_t\}=\{e_s,\,e_t,\,e_s+e_t\}=\Phi_+$.
(ii) $\cos(\pi/5)=\phi/2$, $4c^2-1=\phi^2-1=\phi$; the five listed vectors are positive, pairwise distinct and all have $B$-norm one ($B(e_s+\phi e_t,e_s+\phi e_t)=1+\phi^2-2\phi c=1+\phi^2-\phi^2=1$, and similarly; $B(\phi(e_s+e_t),\phi(e_s+e_t))=\phi^2(2-2c)=\phi^2(2-\phi)=1$). The $N$-sets follow from the same recursion applied along the reduced words $u_k$ as in (2) of [[thm-cg-root-inversion-formulas-and-strong-exchange]], e.g. $N(u_4)=\{e_t\}\sqcup tN(u_3)$ and, for the non-reduced words $u_k$ with $k>5$, from $N(u_{5+j})=\Phi_+\setminus N(u_j')$, which follows from $N(u_5)=\Phi_+$ (equivalently $\rho(u_5)$ exchanges $\Phi_+$ and $\Phi_-$) together with the definition of $N$; the sign patterns are the wall-separation clauses of [[lem-cg-rank-two-prefix-and-chamber-length-induction]] (1).
(iii) Iterating the recurrences: $N((st)^{k+1})=\{e_t\}\sqcup tN((st)^ks)$ and $N((st)^{k+1}s)=\{e_s\}\sqcup sN((st)^{k+1})$, using $t(u)=s(u)=u$ and $t(e_s)=e_s+2e_t=2u-e_s$, $s(e_t)=e_t+2e_s=2u-e_t$, which gives the two formulas by induction on $k$; $\ell((st)^k)=2k$, $\ell((st)^ks)=2k+1$ are the ambient reduced lengths of alternating words ([[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]], or directly by the criterion of [[thm-cg-root-length-criterion-and-faithfulness]] (1)); the open chamber traces are $(j,j+1)$: on the invariant affine line the generators are $y\mapsto-y$ and $y\mapsto2-y$, so $(st)^k$ and $(st)^ks$ give $(-2k,1-2k)$ and $(-2k-1,-2k)$ for all integer $k$. Their positive cones are the open chambers; closed chambers, rather than their interiors, satisfy the supplier's half-plane union.

items.title: An indefinite Coxeter form with a faithful canonical reflection representation
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The Gram matrix and inertia.** By [F1], $[B]=2I-J$, where $Jx=(x_s+x_t+x_r)(1,1,1)$. Put $p=(1,-1,0)$, $q=(1,1,-2)$ and $a=(1,1,1)$ in the coordinates $(e_s,e_t,e_r)$. The coordinate matrix with columns $p,q,a$ has determinant $6\ne0$, so they form a basis. Since $Jp=Jq=0$ and $Ja=3a$, the matrix $2I-J$ has eigenvalues $2,2,-1$ in this basis. Direct substitution into $B(x,y)=2\sum_i x_i y_i-(\sum_i x_i)(\sum_i y_i)$ gives $B(p,p)=4$, $B(q,q)=12$, $B(a,a)=-3$, and all three cross terms zero. Thus $B$ has diagonal matrix $\operatorname{diag}(4,12,-3)$ in this basis, so it is nondegenerate and indefinite with inertia $(2,1,0)$, scalar signature $1$, and positive/negative index pair $(2,1)$. Finally $V_+$ is closed under addition and nonnegative scaling, contains no line because $V_+\cap(-V_+)=\{0\}$, and is not all of $V$ because $-e_s\notin V_+$. This is (i). [F1, F4, algebra]

1.2 **The signs of the computed roots.** By [F2] one has $\ell(s)=1$, $\ell(st)=2$ and $\ell(sts)=3$, so $\ell(st)>\ell(s)$ and $\ell(sts)>\ell(st)$; the length criterion [F3] therefore gives $\rho(s)e_t\in\Phi_+$ and $\rho(st)e_s\in\Phi_+$. By [F1], $\rho(s)e_t=e_t+2e_s$, $\rho(st)e_t=\rho(s)\rho(t)e_t=-\rho(s)e_t=-e_t-2e_s\in\Phi_-$, and $\rho(st)e_s=\rho(s)(e_s+2e_t)=-e_s+2(e_t+2e_s)=3e_s+2e_t$. The signs are consistent with the criterion also in the first two cases because $\ell(stt)=\ell(s)=1<2=\ell(st)$, so $\rho(st)e_t\in\Phi_-$ says exactly that right multiplication by $t$ shortens $st$. [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

1.3 **A nontrivial image.** By [F1], $\rho(r)e_s=e_s+2e_r$, so $\rho(tr)e_s=\rho(t)(e_s+2e_r)=(e_s+2e_t)+2(e_r+2e_t)=e_s+6e_t+2e_r$ and $\rho(str)e_s=\rho(s)(e_s+6e_t+2e_r)=-e_s+6(e_t+2e_s)+2(e_r+2e_s)=15e_s+6e_t+2e_r$. This differs from $e_s$ because its value at $t$ is $6$ while $e_s(t)=0$, so $\rho(str)\ne\mathrm{id}_V$. [F1, F4, algebra]

1.4 **The degenerate rank-two case.** Restrict to $P=\mathbb Re_s+\mathbb Re_t$. By [F1] the Gram matrix of $B|_P$ in $(e_s,e_t)$ is $\begin{pmatrix}1&-1\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}$, and $B(x_se_s+x_te_t,x_se_s+x_te_t)=(x_s-x_t)^2\ge0$, so $B|_P$ is positive semidefinite; its radical is $\{x:B(x,e_s)=B(x,e_t)=0\}=\{x:x_s=x_t\}=\mathbb R(e_s+e_t)$, a line, so $B|_P$ has rank one and in this two-generator case the map $v\mapsto B|_P(v,-)$ from $P$ to $P^*$ has nonzero kernel and is therefore not an identification of $P$ with $P^*$; this does not assert that the original nondegenerate rank-three form has a kernel. [F1, algebra]

1.5 **The free-product assertion.** For each $v\in\{s,t,r\}$, the relation $v^2=1$ defines a homomorphism $\iota_v:\mathbb Z/2\to W$ sending the nonidentity element to $v$. A homomorphism from $\mathbb Z/2$ into any group $H$ is uniquely determined by an element $h_v$ with $h_v^2=1$. Since our Coxeter presentation has no finite off-diagonal relators, its universal property in [F2] gives exactly one homomorphism $W\to H$ sending $v$ to $h_v$ for each $v$. Therefore $(W,\iota_s,\iota_t,\iota_r)$ satisfies the free-product universal property [F5]. [F2, F5, algebra]

2.1 **Faithfulness.** The matrix $m$ is a Coxeter matrix on the finite set $S$, so the homomorphism $\rho:W\to\mathrm{GL}(V)$ is injective by [F3]; this applies to $S$ and to the degenerate two-generator subcase $S'=\{s,t\}$ as well, so in both cases $\rho$ is faithful even though $B$ is indefinite, respectively degenerate. With (i) from 1.1, (ii) from 1.2 and 1.3 together with [F3], and (iii) from 1.4, all clauses are verified: neither indefiniteness nor degeneracy of $B$ obstructs faithfulness. [F3, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 1.4] ∎

items.title: A vector with mixed signs is not a root, while every root has a sign
items.strategy: Direct evaluation. (i) The coordinates of $v$ in the basis $(e_s,e_t)$ are $(1,-1)$ with respect to the ordered basis $(e_s,e_t)$ ([[def-linear-combination-and-span]]); since the basis representation is unique, $v$ is in neither cone. (ii) The sign dichotomy for roots is [[thm-cg-root-sign-and-simple-reflection-positivity]] (2), so $v$ is not a root; the norm computation is $B(v,v)=B(e_s,e_s)-2B(e_s,e_t)+B(e_t,e_t)=2+2c(s,t)$, and [[lem-cg-reflection-representation-descends-and-root-norms]] (3) gives $B(\alpha,\alpha)=1$ for every root $\alpha$. (iii) Substituting $c=\cos(\pi/3)=\frac12$ gives $B(v,v)=3$ and $B(e_s+e_t,e_s+e_t)=2-2c=1$, while $e_s+e_t=\rho(t)e_s$ lies in $\Phi_+$ by the criterion ([[thm-cg-root-sign-and-simple-reflection-positivity]] (2), [[lem-cg-reflection-form-invariance-and-rank-two-orders]]); for $m=\infty$ one has $c=1$ and $B(v,v)=4$. This example marks the exact scope of the sign theorem: it applies to the $W$-orbit of the simple roots, not to arbitrary vectors of $V$.
